page.layout: One block of verse in roman and italic, with Latin elegiac lines set in full measure; below it, right-aligned, the author's name "GOCLE."

main_text.p: Sunt & Apollo mihi, Nymphaq; Coronide nati, Queis delubra magis constituenda reor. Nulla Chelys tā docta fuit, nulla arsq; medendi, Quale opus est medicum docte RODOL-PHE tuum, Quale parentis opus, quo conciliauit amicè Dissimiles inter se, similesq; Sophos. Dicite Pierides lauro hic, an dignior ille[?] Et lauro hic dignus, dignus & ille fuit. Non bene conueniunt discrimina diffona uocū, Nec nisi concordi pectine grata lyra est: Sic nisi conueniant sapientum linguaq;, mensq;, Gratia quanta fuit, gratia tanta perit. Talis inest Patri sapientia, usq; docendi, Per quem iam coeunt, quae coitura neges: Qualis inest Gnato prudentia, usq; medendi, Per quem sanantur, quae moritura putes. Et quia non tantum laudatur acumine Pallas, Quantum laudata est utilitate Dea, Unde oleae inuentrix celebratur dia Minerua, Vsibus humanis commoda multa ferens:

page.notes: Italic passages of the verse were set in italic type; the italic runs are not marked in this transcription. "RODOL-PHE" has a printed break after L. Doubtful: the final word of line 7 ("ille") carries a mark after the e, read as [?]. The mark after "uocū" and the q-abbreviations are read as printed. The top line's "Nymphaq;" carries the -que abbreviation. The word "Dea" is printed with a stroke, read as Dea.
